questions.knowledge_point: Determining a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
questions.problem:
What is the linear transformation $T$ whose standard matrix is 
$T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}].$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}x+z \\ -y+z \\ x-y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,T\,$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+z \\ -y+z \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
What is the linear transformation $T$ whose standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 4 \\ 5 & 3 & -2 \\ 1 & -6 & 7\end{aligned}]?$

| $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}].$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 4 \\ 5 & 3 & -2 \\ 1 & -6 & 7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x-y+4z \\ 5x+3y-2z \\ x-6y+7z\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,T\,$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y+4z \\ 5x+3y-2z \\ x-6y+7z\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T,$ find $T(v).$

| $T(v)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 0 & -1 \\ 4 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T,$ find $T(v).$

| $T(v)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 0 & -1 \\ 4 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -6 \\ 14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation With Rearranging
questions.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-6x \\ 5y+9x\end{aligned}].
$$

| $T=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-6x \\ 9x+5y\end{aligned}]
$$

We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6x \\ 9x+5y\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}-6 & 0 \\ 9 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6x \\ 9x+5y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}-6 & 0 \\ 9 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
